JUDGMENT SHEET
IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT
LAHORE
(JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT)
MUHAMMAD WAHEED KHAN, J.- Appellant, Nadeem
Ali has challenged conviction and sentence awarded to him by the
learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kasur, vide judgment dated
31.10.2024, passed in case FIR No.957 dated 13.12.2022 registered u/s
302 PPC at Police Station A-Division Kasur, whereby he was
convicted under section 302(b) PPC and sentenced to imprisonment
for life. He was also directed to pay Rs.2,00,000/- as compensation u/s
544-A Cr.P.C. to the legal heirs of deceased Naseem Bibi, in default
thereof, to further undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six
months. Benefit u/s 382-B Cr.P.C. was also extended to him.
2. Safia Begum complainant of the case, while submitting
application (Ex-PB) to the police narrated facts of the case as under;-
“That on 12.12.2022, the wedding ceremonies of her maternal
granddaughter and grandson were scheduled to take place. During
Mehndi function, her daughter, Naseem Bibi, informed her that
accused, Nadeem Ali, had used abusive language with her over the
issue of wedding expenses, whereupon she (complainant) assured
her daughter that she would bear all the said expenses. On the
night between 12.12.2022 and 13.12.2022, at about 03:00 a.m.,
Cr. Appeal No.188-J of 2025
Nadeem Ali v. The State, etc.
JUDGMENT
body: Date of hearing 10.11.2026 Appellant by Mr. Shahid Rafiq Mayo, Advocate.
State by Ms. Noshe Malik, Deputy Prosecutor General.
Complainant by Nemo.
(Nadeem Ali v. The State, etc.)

she accompanied her daughter, Naseem Bibi, to her house. On the same date, at about 05:00 a.m., accused, Nadeem Ali, called Naseem Bibi, who went to the upper portion of the house to hand over clothes to him. In the meantime, she heard the cries of her daughter, on which she alongwith her grandsons, Zeeshan and Muhammad Usman, and granddaughter, Maria Bibi, rushed to the upper portion, where they allegedly saw that accused Nadeem Ali was strangulating Naseem Bibi with her dupatta, while she was lying on a cot. As a result, Naseem Bibi died at the spot. Upon seeing the complainant and the other witnesses, the accused fled from the spot. The motive behind the occurrence was that the deceased had demanded wedding expenses from the accused.”

3. After registration of formal FIR, the matter was investigated and on culmination of the case, report u/s 173 Cr.P.C. was submitted before the learned trial Court, while declaring the appellant as guilty, whereby he was summoned to face trial. Formal charge was framed, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. The prosecution in order to prove its case produced as many as eleven witnesses. Ocular account was furnished by complainant Safia Bibi (PW-2), her grandsons Shan alias Zeeshan (PW-3), Muhammad Usman (PW-9) and granddaughter, Maria Bibi (PW-10). Medical evidence was furnished by Dr. Amina Rehman (PW-11), who conducted postmortem examination of the deceased. Rasheed Shahzad Inspector, who conducted investigation of the case, appeared as PW-7. The remaining witnesses were formal in nature and prosecution after producing certain documents closed its evidence. After completion of prosecution evidence, statement of the appellant was recorded u/s 342 Cr.P.C., in which he denied all the allegations leveled against him by the prosecution. Neither he appeared as his own witness u/s 340 (2) Cr.P.C., nor produced any evidence in his defence. After evaluating prosecution evidence available on record, learned trial Court found the prosecution version correct beyond any shadow of doubt, which resulted into conviction and sentence of the appellant in the afore stated terms.

4. In support of the instant appeal, learned counsel for the appellant has contended that case of the prosecution is inherently flawed, hence, fails to inspire confidence; that the matter was reported to the police (Nadeem Ali v. The State, etc.)

with unexplained delay of about ten hours, which made the prosecution story doubtful; that the witnesses of the ocular account were not trusted ones as their statements were full of contradictions and even otherwise, they were closely related to the deceased, so, their evidence cannot be relied upon to maintain conviction and sentence and that too, in an offence having capital punishment; that medical evidence was not in line with the ocular account; that motive set up by the prosecution was not proved and as such same was disbelieved by the learned trial Court; that nothing was recovered from possession of the appellant during the course of investigation; that the impugned judgment is based on surmises and conjectures as material evidence available on record in favour of the appellant has been mis-read by the prosecution and lastly prays that since the prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case against the appellant up to hilt, hence, by accepting the instant appeal, he be acquitted of the charge.

5. Conversely, learned Deputy Prosecutor General has faithfully defended the impugned judgment by controverting the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and has contended that the prosecution has ably proved its case against the appellant “beyond reasonable shadow of doubt”; that to substantiate the case of the prosecution inmates of the house deposed before the learned trial Court and their evidence cannot be discarded on any hypotheses; the medical evidence was fully supportive in nature; that sufficient evidence was adduced to prove motive part of the incident, so, all the evidence produced by the prosecution fully corroborates the ocular version, so, in presence of voluminous evidence, the appellant does not deserve any leniency and he has rightly been adjudged guilty by the learned trial Court, hence, the instant appeal is liable to be dismissed.

6. I have heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned Law Officer, perused the record with their assistance and noticed that the unfortunate incident, wherein daughter of the complainant, namely, Naseem Bibi (deceased) was done to death, allegedly by accused Nadeem Ali (Nadeem Ali v. The State, etc.)

(appellant) took place in the early morning of 13.12.2022 at 05:00 a.m. in the area of Kachi Abadi Paras Road Saithi Colony Kasur, whereas the distance between crime scene and the Police Station, is mentioned as one kilometer towards east and the matter was reported to the police with the delay of ten hours and five munities at 03:05 p.m. on the same day. Learned counsel for the appellant has contended that the said delay, particularly in view of the short distance between the place of occurrence and the police station, afforded sufficient opportunity to the complainant party to deliberate and fabricate a false version, thereby casting serious doubt on the prosecution case. I have considered this contention in the light of the available record. It is well settled that delay in lodging the FIR is not, in every case, fatal to the prosecution, nevertheless, where such delay remains unexplained, it assumes significance, as it may provide an opportunity for consultation, deliberation and subsequent embellishment of the prosecution version. The effect of delay, therefore, has to be assessed in the context of the facts and circumstances of each case, particularly the possibility of substitution or false implication of the accused. In the present case, the prosecution has nominated only one accused in the FIR, and no previous enmity or dispute between the appellant and the deceased has been brought on record. These circumstances may be considered while assessing the possibility of deliberation or false implication, however, they do not, by themselves, furnish an explanation for the delay of ten hours and five minutes. The mere absence of an apparent motive for false implication cannot automatically render an unexplained delay inconsequential. The delay must, therefore, be evaluated along with the ocular account and other evidence available on record. Meaning thereby that mere delay in lodging of FIR is never fatal for the prosecution in absence of any allegation of substitution or concoction as the prosecution has gained nothing by this delay. Reliance is placed on the judgment passed in case titled “MUHAMMAD AJAIB”
. The Muhammad Ajaib v. EHBOOB KHAN and another (PLJ 2000 SC (AJ&K) 192) (Nadeem Ali v. The State, etc.)
august Supreme Court of Pakistan in case titled “MUHAMMAD GUL”
, had held that unexplained delay in lodging the FIR is not fatal in all cases.

7. The ocular account in the present case has been furnished by Safia Bibi (PW-2), complainant and mother of the deceased, Shan alias Zeeshan (PW-3) and Muhammad Usman (PW-9), sons of the deceased and Maria Bibi (PW-10), daughter of the deceased. While appearing before the learned trial Court as PW-2, Safia Bibi deposed that, on the fateful morning of 13.12.2022, at about 05:00 a.m., upon hearing the cries of Naseem Bibi (deceased), she, along with Shan alias Zeeshan (PW-3), Muhammad Usman (PW-9) and Maria Bibi (PW-10), rushed to the upper storey of the house, where they saw the appellant, Nadeem Ali, strangulating Naseem Bibi by wrapping her dupatta around her neck, which caused her death. Shan alias Zeeshan (PW-3), while appearing as a witness, substantially corroborated the stance taken by the complainant in his examination-in-chief. It is, however, noteworthy that Shan alias Zeeshan (PW-3), during his cross-examination, as well as the other two eye-witnesses, namely, Muhammad Usman (PW-9) and Maria Bibi (PW-10), during their respective examinations-in-chief, deposed that the appellant, Nadeem Ali, was their real father and that they had forgiven him in the name of Allah Almighty, requesting that he be acquitted. Significantly, none of these witnesses disowned the prosecution version or stated that the appellant had not committed the murder of their mother, Naseem Bibi, or that he had been falsely implicated in the case. Their expressions of forgiveness and request for acquittal, therefore, cannot, by themselves, be construed as a retraction from their earlier stance. Had the legal heirs intended to enter into a compromise, the matter would have been required to be brought before the Court through an appropriate application, to be considered in accordance with law. Even otherwise, complainant, Safia Bibi (PW-2), being the real mother of the deceased and one of her legal heirs, has . MUHAMMAD GUL v. The STATE” (1970 SCMR 797)
(Nadeem Ali v. The State, etc.)

fully supported the prosecution case. Her testimony remained consistent with regard to the date, time, place, mode and manner of the occurrence. Her evidence inspires confidence and is also in consonance with the probabilities and other circumstances of the case. Despite being subjected to lengthy cross-examination by learned defence counsel, nothing material could be elicited from her testimony to discredit her account or create a dent in the prosecution case.

8. The prosecution in order to further strengthen its case adduced medical evidence in the shape of testimony of Dr. Amina Rehman, who while appearing in the dock as PW-11, testified that she conducted postmortem examination of the deceased on 13.12.2022 at 04:50 p.m. and during autopsy, on examination of neck of the deceased and description of injuries, she (PW-11) observed as under;- Examination of Neck Congestion in surrounding nostuls were blood shined hyoid bone was fractured froth from mouth.
Description of injuries.

Mark around neck slight congestion, slight congestion below neck area. According to the opinion of said Medical Officer, death of the deceased was caused by strangulation, injury caused suffocation asphyxia and ultimately shock causing death. It shows that death of the deceased was caused by asphyxia, which fact corroborates the ocular account furnished by the prosecution.

9. It is also noticed that during the course of investigation, buccal swabs (Item No.1) of Naseem Bibi (deceased), right and left hands nail swabs (Items Nos. 2 & 3 respectively), one cotton swab (Item No.4) from the place of occurrence, one multi coloured piece of cloth (dupatta) found wrapped around the neck of the deceased (Item No.5), swab taken from the piece of cloth (Item No.5.1), stain sections taken from the piece of cloth (Items No.5.2-5.3), hair found on piece of cloth (Item No.5.4), one black coloured gents “qameez” purportedly of suspect, having suspected blood stain on right sleeve, found on (Nadeem Ali v. The State, etc.)

washroom at first floor of house at crime scene (Item No.6), stain sections taken from the said ‘qameez’ (Items Nos.6.1-6.3) and buccal swab standards of Nadeem Ali (appellant), were taken by the Investigating Agency and sent for DNA analysis. According to the results and conclusion of report (Ex-PM), furnished by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA), the DNA profile obtained from item No.3 (left hands nail swabs), item No.5.1 (swab taken from the piece of cloth) and item No.5.3 (stain section taken from the piece of cloth) are mixtures of at least two individuals. Naseem Bibi (item No.1) and Nadeem Ali (item No. S1) cannot be excluded as being contributors to this DNA mixture profile. Meaning thereby that medical evidence as well as the evidence in shape of the DNA report (Ex-PM), are fully suggestive of the fact that the appellant was the real culprit, who committed the occurrence.

10. Although DNA report, conclusively connects the appellant, with the crime but the same evidence (DNA evidence) per se may not considered sufficient, to award and maintain conviction of the appellant under the afore referred provision of law (offence u/s 302 PPC). I have gone through the different provisions of law i.e. Articles 59 and 164 of the Qanoon-i-Shahadat Order, 1984 (QSO), Sections 164-B/510 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Cr.P.C.) and Section 9 of Punjab Forensic Science Agency Act, 2007 and various case laws developed upon the subject including cases of “SALMAN AKRAM” and “ALI HAIDER alias PAPU”

. There is no denial of the fact that the evidence which has become available because of modern devices is made admissible and later on, through insertion of proviso with Article 164 of QSO, through enactment IV of 2017 dated 16.02.2017, it was enacted that conviction on the basis of modern devices or techniques may be lawful. Then there could be another objection qua per se admissibility of the DNA report as under section 510 Cr.P.C., there is “SALMAN AKRAM RAJA and another v. GOVERNMENT OF PUNJAB through Chief Secretary and others” (2013 SCMR 203)
“ALI HAIDER alias PAPU v. JAMEEL HUSSAIN and others”(PLD 2021 Supreme Court 362) (Nadeem Ali v. The State, etc.)

no mention regarding the DNA report. However, to overcome this deficiency and non-providing the DNA report in section 510 Cr.P.C., which made certain reports based on the expert opinion per se admissible, a new legislation in the form of sub-section (3) of section 9 of the Punjab Forensic Science Agency Act, 2007 (Act), has been made, which is reproduced as under;- 9. Experts.– (1) ….

(2) … (3) A person appointed in the Agency as an expert shall be deemed as an expert appointed under section 510 of the Code and a person specially skilled in a forensic material under Article 59 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (X of 1984).

(4) …… So, there should be hardly any dispute or skepticism about its per se admissibility as this anomaly has been resolved by introducing a special enactment through Sub-section (3) of section 9 of the Act supra. Even otherwise, the august Supreme Court of Pakistan in supura case of Salman Akram Raja’s case, administration of DNA and preservation of DNA evidence have been made mandatory in rape cases. The august Supreme Court of Pakistan in case of “ALI HAIDER alias PAPU, supra, on one hand, declared the DNA evidence as a gold standard to establish the identity of an accused and acknowledged the significant stature of technological and scientific tools, devices and techniques that help provide objective, credible and reliable evidences relating to Court cases, for reaching to judicious decisions and also ordained therein that Courts must be open to developments in forensic science and embrace new techniques and devices to resolve a dispute, provided the said technique and device were well established and widely accepted in the scientific community as a credible and reliable technique or device, but stopping short of designating it as independent or primary evidence, and reckoned the same, one of the strongest corroborative piece of evidence.
(Nadeem Ali v. The State, etc.)

11. So far as the motive part of the incident is concerned, the occurrence allegedly took place in the backdrop of the motive that the deceased was demanding wedding expenses from the appellant due to which, dispute arose between them and the appellant committed her murder. Suffice it to say that the prosecution has failed to prove this piece of evidence and the motive set up by the prosecution remained mere oral assertions of the prosecution witnesses, resultantly, this piece of evidence did not provide any corroboration to the ocular account.

12. As a sequel to above discussion, the conclusion is inevitable that the prosecution has proved its case by producing trust worthy, confidence inspiring and credible ocular account, which has also been supported and corroborated by the other pieces of evidence i.e. medical evidence, DNA report (Ex-PM) furnished by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA), but keeping in view the fact that motive part of the incident remained unproved and the fact that all the legal heirs of the deceased except the complainant have forgiven the appellant, therefore, on these grounds, capital punishment of the appellant was withheld by the learned trial Court. I have gone through the impugned judgment as well and found that observations and findings so made therein, appear to be convincing and reasonable in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, therefore, arguments of learned counsel for the appellant, being devoid of any force are repelled accordingly and held that the appellant has rightly been convicted by the learned trial Court. Hence, the instant appeal is dismissed and the conviction and sentence awarded to the appellant by the learned trial Court are maintained. Benefit under section 382-B Cr.P.C. as observed by the learned trial Court will remain intact.
(MUHAMMAD WAHEED KHAN)
